consumer: VCO-A hard-synced triangle, reset every 256 samples (tap dryA)
source_evidence: product-reachable MECHANISM, precision-set rate: vco_a.sync_in is a registered, patchable jack (registry descriptor threshold 5.0V / hysteresis 0.2V; no consumer before task #111). Stimulus = LFO-A square (lfo_a_wave=0) patched to vco_a.sync_in through the public MachineRuntime::connect, so the patch is a panel-reachable cable, not a test-only injection surface. Rate: lfo_a_rate = sr/(M*10) Hz with lfo_a_speed_mult index 2 (= x10, machine_runtime.h speedMultFromIndex_), giving an effective sr/M Hz -> one rising edge every EXACTLY M samples (M=256 at 44.1/48k, 512 at 88.2/96k) and a per-sample phase step of exactly 1/M; 17.23-18.75 Hz sits inside the LFO's 0.1..20 Hz panel range. The edge therefore lands ON a sample-grid point; the exact Hz is set from canonical state by the probe (a panel user dials it approximately). The slave is the SAME dry_a-tapped VCO-A triangle arm as vco_a_tri. Exact M-periodicity of the produced signal and the measured cycle anchor are ASSERTED by the analyzer (blsync_per / blsync_off), which fails closed to no-column rather than answering if the premise does not hold.
